s: I like apples, and I also like rice.
Apples are fruit, rice is not fruit.
At noon I eat rice, not apples.
Both apples and rice are good.
Mom bought a lot of apples and rice.
This store is big, that store is small.
The big store has a lot of things, the small store has few things.
I like going to the big store to buy things.
The small store doesn't have many people, and I like that too.
Today my mom and I go to the store to buy apples.
In the morning, my friend comes to my home.
I drink milk, he drinks soy milk.
We eat bread, and also eat eggs.
Breakfast is delicious, we are very happy.
We ate breakfast, then go to school.
This afternoon, I go to the store to buy fruit.
There is a lot of fruit in the store — there are big apples and small apples.
I say, "How much is one apple?"
The person at the store says, "Big apples are three kuai each, and small apples are one kuai each."
I go home and eat the apples with my mom — the apples are delicious.
China has many people, and also many delicious dishes.
I live in Beijing, and I like Beijing a lot.
Tomorrow I am taking a plane to Shanghai.
China has many big cities, and I want to go see all of them.
China is very big, and I don't have much time.
My dad works at a store.
He goes to the store at seven in the morning.
At noon he does not go home; he eats at the store.
At six in the evening, he goes home.
Dad is very busy, and he likes his job a lot.
I also want to go take a look at his store.
My family has a dog, and also has a cat.
The dog is big, the cat is small.
The dog likes to eat, the cat likes to drink water.
Both the dog and the cat are pretty.
I like the dog a lot, and I also like the cat a lot.
Today the weather is very good, and we are driving to Beijing.
It is nine in the morning now, and we are very happy.
Beijing has our friend; his name is Wang Ming.
We want to go to his home to drink tea.
Wang Ming says, "You've come, that's wonderful!"
There are three people in my family: Dad, Mom, and me.
At noon we eat at home.
Mom made a lot of dishes and rice.
I ate a lot of rice and drank a cup of water.
This morning, I'm outside, and I see a teacher.
I say, "Teacher, excuse me, what time is it now?"
The teacher says, "It's seven o'clock now."
I love studying Chinese, and Chinese numbers are really fun!
Look — one, two, and three are all easy to write.
Ten and one make eleven; ten and two make twelve.
I'm thirty this year, and my daughter is three.
She can already say lots of numbers, which makes us all very happy.
Can you write numbers in Chinese?
At five in the afternoon, dad comes home.
We are all at home, and we are very happy.
The food mom made is delicious, and we are all very happy.
In the afternoon I go to the shop with Mom.
There are a lot of things in the shop.
We buy six apples and some water.
The apples are ten kuai, and the water is three kuai.
Mom says: "These apples are very good."
I really like going to the shop with Mom.
The teacher is very good, and I like the teacher a lot.
I'm very happy to have met the teacher.
This morning, I see my teacher and say, "Good morning, teacher!"
At school, I see my classmate, and we say, "Hello!"
At noon, I see the doctor and say, "Hello, how are you?"
The doctor says, "I'm very good, thank you!"
In the afternoon, I see a man and a woman, and we say, "Hello!"
Now, I go home and say, "Mom, goodbye!"
This morning, I see my friend Xiaomei at school.
Xiaomei looks at me and says, "I'm very good, and you?"
I say, "I'm very good too, thank you."
Xiaomei says, "Let's go drink tea together, OK?"
I say, "Sure!" We go drink tea together.
This afternoon, my mom and I go to the store to buy things.
I see some pretty clothes, and I say, "How much are these clothes?"
The store clerk says, "These clothes are thirty kuai."
Mom sees a cup, and she says, "How much is one cup?"
We buy the things, take a taxi home, and I say, "How much?"
My friend says, "How old are you this year?"
I say, "I am twenty years old this year."
I also say, "How old are you this year?"
My friend says, "I am twenty-one years old this year."
She is older, I am younger, and we are both very happy.
Mom says: "Let's go to the hospital."
The doctor takes a look at me.
The doctor says: "Please drink more water and sleep more."
Tomorrow I want to go to school.
Today, I'm in China, and I see a person.
That person speaks Chinese, but I can't understand him.
I say, "Sorry, I can't speak Chinese."
I say, "I'm a student, and I'm learning Chinese."
That person says, "It's okay, go ahead and speak. What's your name?"
I tell him my name, and he says, "Your Chinese is good."
My name is Li Ming, and I really love sleeping.
There is a cat at my home — the cat and I both love sleeping.
This morning I slept, at noon I slept, and in the afternoon I want to sleep.
Mom says, "You may not sleep now — go study!"
When I read my book, my cat sleeps on my book.
I am very happy — my cat is so great!
Tomorrow I'm going to Beijing to study.
Mom looks at my clothes and books and says, "You'll be in Beijing and I'll be at home. I'll miss you."
I like school and I like my friends — but it's my mom and dad I love.
I am American, and I work in China.
I can speak a little Chinese.
Today at noon I go to a restaurant to eat.
I say, "I'll have rice and tea."
The man at the restaurant hears this and is very pleased; he says, "Your Chinese is very good!"
I am very happy — I love studying Chinese.
This morning the weather was lovely, and I wanted to go shopping.
At noon it started to rain, so I couldn't go to the shop anymore.
I watched TV at home and drank a cup of hot tea.
My cat slept on the chair.
In the afternoon the rain stopped and the weather turned nice again.
My dog and I went to the shop to buy things, and we were both very happy.
I want to go to school, where are my keys?
The keys are not on the table.
The keys are also not on the chair.
I ask mom, "Have you seen my keys?"
Mom says, "The keys are inside your backpack."
I see the keys, I am very happy.
In the evening, we eat at home.
Mom says this dish is delicious.
Mom is very happy, and I am very happy too.
My mom is a wonderful cook.
Today at noon she made three dishes.
The rice was hot and the food was delicious.
Dad said, "The food your mom makes is just so delicious!"
I ate a lot, and I was very happy.
I love my mom, and I love her cooking too.
My friend asks, "What's the date today?"
My friend says, "September 5th? My birthday is September 15th!"
I say, "My birthday is September 20th — both our birthdays are in September."
My friend says, "On September 15th, come over to my place!"
My family has a little cat called Mimi.
Mimi is very small and loves to sleep.
At noon when I eat, it sits on my chair.
In the afternoon it likes to watch the little dogs outside.
Mimi is my good friend — I love it very much.
I'm not Chinese — I study Mandarin at school.
My Chinese teacher is from Beijing.
Yesterday she gave me a Chinese name: Mingyue.
She said, "Ming is the ming in 'tomorrow', and yue is the yue in 'January'."
I love this name, and now my friends all call me Mingyue.
I have a computer; the computer is on the desk.
I watch movies on the computer.
I also read books on the computer.
In the afternoon we watch TV together.
I have a cup — it was my mom who bought it.
The cup is not big and is very pretty — there is a little cat on it.
In the morning, there is tea in my cup; in the afternoon, there is water.
When the weather is cold, I love drinking hot tea.
Today my classmate looks at my cup and says, "Your cup is so pretty!"
I say, "It was my mom who bought it." We are both very happy.
I get up at seven o'clock.
At noon I eat with my friends.
In the afternoon I study at home.
In the evening I read, and at eleven I go to bed.
My family has a little dog called Doudou.
Doudou is two years old and loves to eat.
Every morning it goes running with me.
When I come home, it gets very happy.
I love Doudou — it is my good friend.
There are four people in my family.
My dad is a doctor, and my mom is a teacher.
I have a younger sister; she is eight years old this year.
We all love the food my mom cooks.
I have a good friend called Li Yue.
Li Yue is a doctor; she works at a hospital.
She loves reading, and she also loves cooking.
The food she makes is delicious, and we are both very happy.
Today I go to the store to buy things.
One book costs twenty yuan, and I bought one.
I also bought fruit, ten yuan.
Now I don't have much money left.
I won't buy anything more; I am going home.
My room isn't big, but it's very pretty.
In the room there is a desk and a chair.
On the desk there is a computer and some books.
I like to sit on the chair, reading and writing characters.
My cat likes to sleep in my room.
I am a student, and my school is big.
There are many classmates and teachers in the school.
In the morning we study Chinese, and in the afternoon we read and write characters.
My teacher is very nice, and the classmates are all happy.
In front of the school there is a small shop, and I like to go there to buy water.
I love my school very much.
Teacher Li is my Chinese teacher.
She is in her thirties and very pretty.
She speaks Chinese, and also a little English.
When we can't write characters, she teaches us how.
Today, our class has a new classmate.
Her name is Xiaomei, she is Chinese.
I ask her, "How old are you this year?"
She says, "I am ten years old."
We sit together, and study together.
I am very happy to meet her.
Today at school, I see a classmate; her name is Xiaomei.
I say, "My name is Wang Xiaoming. Nice to meet you!"
She says, "Nice to meet you too! What's your nationality?"
I say, "I'm Chinese. What about you?"
She says, "I'm Chinese too — we're classmates, and friends as well."
I'm on a plane right now, going to Beijing to see a friend.
The plane is big, and there are a lot of people on board.
I read my book and watch a movie too.
The flight attendant says, "Sir, what would you like to drink?"
I say, "A cup of tea, thank you!"
At three in the afternoon the plane arrives in Beijing, and I'm so happy.
Yesterday afternoon, I missed my mom very much.
I made a phone call and said, "Hello, Mom, how are you?"
Mom said, "I'm fine! Have you eaten yet?"
I said, "I have. I'm studying Chinese at school, and I'm very happy."
Mom said, "Good. Come home for a meal on Sunday, okay?"
My friend comes to my home, and I am very happy.
I ask my friend to sit, and offer him tea.
My friend sat down, and drank the tea.
My friend says thank you, and I say you're welcome.
We talk, and are very happy.
There are many pretty clothes in the shop.
Mom really likes that pretty piece of clothing.
She says, "How much is this piece of clothing?"
Mom bought that pretty piece of clothing, and she is very happy.
My friend is called Wang Xiaoming, and he really loves reading books.
He has many books at home — there are books on the table and books on the chair.
On Sundays he does not work; he reads books at home.
I say, "How many books do you have?" He says, "Many, many!"
He says, "There are many good things inside books — do you read?"
Now, on Sundays he and I both read books at home.
At noon we go to a restaurant to eat.
I order a bowl of rice and some dishes.
My friend drinks water; I drink tea.
The food is delicious, and we are all very happy.
The restaurant staff says: "Welcome back again!"
This afternoon, I'm at home making a phone call.
I say, "Hello, are you my classmate?"
The person says, "No, you dialed the wrong number."
I say, "Sorry, I dialed the wrong number."
The person says, "It's okay, it's okay."
It's raining today, and I don't have an umbrella.
My classmate says, "I have an umbrella, let's go home together."
I'm very happy, and I say, "Thank you!"
My classmate says, "You're welcome, we're friends."
We go home together; the weather is very cold, but I'm very happy.
Hello! My name is Wang Xiaoming.
I am a student, twenty years old this year.
My family is my dad, my mom and me.
I like reading books and watching movies.
In the afternoon I go to the store to buy something.
I want to buy a cup.
This cup is very pretty — how much is it?
I really like my new cup.
Our teacher is Chinese, and she is very nice.
In the morning we learn to write Chinese characters.
The characters I write are not very good, but the teacher says it doesn't matter.
At four in the afternoon, we go home.
Today is Sunday — I don't work, and I'm very happy.
In the morning I stay home, drinking tea and reading.
At noon my friend and I go to a restaurant, and the food is delicious.
In the afternoon we go to see a movie.
This morning I am going to the train station.
I ask the driver: "How much is it?"
Twenty minutes later, I see the train station.
Tomorrow, I want to take the train to Beijing.
There are many people at the train station.
My train is at nine o'clock.
There are many seats on the train.
I read a book on the train, I am very happy.
In the morning I like to drink coffee; in the afternoon I like to drink tea.
Today a friend comes to my home.
I say, "Would you like tea or coffee?"
He says, "I don't drink coffee — I love hot tea."
We drink tea together, and we are both very happy.
The weather today is way too hot!
I don't want to work — I just want to drink water.
I drank three cups of water and ate a big apple.
My dog is hot too and doesn't want to eat anything.
In the afternoon we won't go to the shop — we'll watch a movie at home.
What will the weather be like tomorrow? I think it won't be too hot!
My friend got sick, he is at the hospital.
This afternoon, I go to the hospital to see him.
The hospital is big, there are many people inside.
I see him, I am very happy.
He says, "Thank you for coming to see me."
Today is Saturday, and I don't have to work.
In the afternoon, my friend and I went to see a movie.
The movie was really good, and we both loved it.
While watching the movie, we drank tea and ate apples.
The people in the movie spoke Chinese, and I could catch a little of it!
Tomorrow I want to watch another movie.
The weather is great today — not cold and not hot.
It rained yesterday, but today it has stopped.
My mom and I go out for a walk.
There are lots of people outside, all having fun.
This is my cup — I really love drinking tea.
What is that? That is my book.
My book is a Chinese book — I am studying Chinese.
My desk is small, but my computer is big.
How about you? What things do you have?
In the morning I am sleeping, and Mom calls me.
I say, "What time is it now?"
Mom says, "It's eight o'clock! You go to work at nine!"
I don't eat breakfast — I just drink a little water.
At 8:40 I take a taxi to work.
Tomorrow I will get up at seven!
At school I got to know a classmate.
I say: "My name is Wang Xiaoming. And you?"
He says: "My name is Li Ming."
He is twenty years old and is Chinese.
I live in Beijing — Beijing is very big.
My home is not big, but my cat is very pretty.
I love going to restaurants to eat rice and good food.
Tomorrow my friend is coming to my home, and I am very happy.
Would you like to come to Beijing?
He is my friend, and he is a Chinese teacher.
He works at a school and has many students.
He has a daughter, and she is five years old.
His daughter is little — she loves books and TV.
They are both my good friends.
I study Chinese, and I really love writing Chinese characters.
This morning, the teacher says, "Let's write Chinese characters, okay?"
I write 大, 小, and 人 — these characters are easy to write.
The characters I write are not very pretty; the teacher says, "It doesn't matter!"
The teacher says, "Write more, and your characters can be very pretty."
Now I write Chinese characters at home, and I am very happy.
My classmate asks, "Are you a student?" I say, "Yes, I am a student."
My classmate asks, "Do you have a cat?" I say, "No, I have a dog."
My classmate asks, "Can you speak Chinese?" I say, "I can, and I like it."
My classmate asks, "Do you like cats?" I say, "No, I like dogs."
My classmate says, "Your Chinese is good!"
Yesterday it rained and the weather was cold, so I stayed home and read.
Today it isn't raining, and the weather is lovely.
In the morning I went to school to study, and at noon I ate rice with my classmates.
Tomorrow is Sunday, so I won't go to school.
I want to go to the store to buy some clothes.
Yesterday, today, and tomorrow — I'm happy every day.
Today is my birthday, and I'm very happy.
In the morning, my family all said to me, "Happy birthday!"
At noon, my friends treated me to a meal, and we sang songs together.
In the afternoon, we went to the park to hang out, and the weather was nice too.
In the evening, mom made a big cake, and the whole family ate cake together.
Everyone gave me lots of gifts, and I was extremely happy.
This was really a happy day!
Saturday morning, I was still sleeping.
My friend called me: "It's already ten o'clock — why aren't you up yet?"
As soon as I heard that, I got up right away.
We were supposed to meet at the cinema entrance at ten thirty.
I only had twenty minutes, and I was so anxious.
I didn't eat breakfast — I took a taxi straight to the cinema.
When I got to the entrance, my friend was already there waiting for me.
This afternoon I went to visit my friend's new home.
But after walking for ten minutes, I couldn't find the way anymore.
I asked a man nearby, "Excuse me, how do I get to Beijing Road?"
He said, "Go straight ahead, turn left at the traffic light, and you're there."
I asked him, "Is it far from here?"
He said with a smile, "Not far — a five-minute walk and you're there."
Soon I arrived at my friend's home, and he was very happy to see me.
At eight in the evening, we arrived at our hotel in Beijing.
The attendant asked: "Hello, sir, what is your name?"
I told him my name, and he gave us a big room.
The room is big and new; we both like it a lot.
My wife said she was tired and wanted to rest.
I drank a cup of tea, glanced at my phone, and then went to sleep.
I bought my phone five years ago — it's really old.
It's so slow that while I wait for it, I can finish a whole cup of tea.
So yesterday afternoon I went to the shop to look at new phones.
The shop assistant said: "This is this year's newest phone — we have it in white and in black."
I asked: "Is it faster than my old phone?"
The assistant said with a smile: "Much faster — and it's not expensive!"
I bought a black one — my wallet is lighter now, but I'm really happy!
Tomorrow my friend and I are taking the train to Beijing, so we go to the station to buy tickets.
The clerk asks, "Where are you going?"
I say, "To Beijing — two tickets for the nine o'clock, please."
The clerk checks and says, "The nine o'clock is sold out. Would ten work?"
I check with my friend, who says, "That's fine — ten isn't late either."
The clerk says, "Alright — two tickets, forty kuai in total."
We buy the tickets, and on the way out my friend says, "Let's get here a bit early tomorrow."
In the morning I go to the coffee shop to buy coffee.
The server asks me: "Would you like it hot or iced?"
I say: "I'd like a hot coffee, no sugar."
The coffee is thirty kuai — a little expensive.
But it's delicious — I want to drink it every day.
Yesterday was my birthday — I turned thirty.
In the evening my friends came to my home, and we ate and sang together.
My wife made me a very big cake.
I said: "Thank you, everyone! I hope we can celebrate my birthday together again next year!"
Although I'm already thirty, I feel like I'm still twenty!
This morning I went to a store to buy clothes.
I saw a white top — very pretty, but it cost three hundred kuai.
I asked the shop assistant: "Do you have a slightly cheaper one?"
She gave me a black top — one hundred fifty kuai, cheaper than the white one.
The black top was also very pretty, so I bought it.
I think cheap things can be pretty too.
My daughter is seven this year, and she's in first grade.
Every morning, Mom takes her to school.
Her schoolbag is very heavy — inside there are lots of books and notebooks.
At school, she has made many new friends, and she also likes her teacher.
After school, she likes doing homework together with her friends.
She says, "I really like going to school — school is very interesting."
Saturday morning, mom said the room was too messy and told me to clean it up.
First I tidied the books on the desk, then picked up the clothes on the floor.
After cleaning for an hour, I felt both tired and hungry.
Mom looked at the room and smiled, saying: "You cleaned it really well!"
I also wiped the windows a bit, and the room became brighter.
Because the room was clean, my mood also got better.
Mom said if I clean every week, the room won't get so messy.
My company is very close to my home — it only takes ten minutes to walk.
Every day I don't need to take a car or ride a bicycle — I can just walk to work.
My coworker lives far away — every day he has to ride in the car for an hour.
He often says he really wants to live near the company.
I don't need to get up early — I feel very lucky.
After I get off work, I'm home very quickly, so I can rest a bit earlier.
One evening I was at home doing homework when someone called out at my door.
From outside, she says: "It's me, your classmate."
I smile, walk to the door, and say: "Please come in, please sit!"
My classmate comes in, sees there are lots of books on my table, and says: "Are you busy?"
I say: "Not too busy, let's do homework together."
She sits down and says: "Okay, let's get started!"
This evening my wife and I cooked together.
She washed the vegetables and I made the eggs and the fish.
While I was cooking, she drank tea next to me.
She said: "The fish is almost ready — don't cook it too long."
While we were eating, she said today's food was tastier than the restaurant's.
Cooking is a little tiring, but cooking together with my wife makes me happy.
On Saturday, I went to visit my friend's home.
My friend's mom had made lots of dishes — there was fish, and soup too.
I ate a piece of the fish and said, "That's really good!"
My friend said, "If you like it, eat some more."
I ate a lot more — everything was so delicious.
When I left, I told my friend, "Your mom's cooking is even better than a restaurant's."
It's raining in the afternoon, and my family doesn't have an umbrella.
I go to a nearby store and ask the clerk: "Do you have umbrellas here?"
I go to the nearby supermarket again and ask: "Do you have umbrellas here?"
The supermarket clerk says: "Yes, this one is thirty yuan."
I pay, and carrying my new umbrella, I walk home.
I'm traveling in China, but I don't know how to get to the train station.
I ask someone: "Hello, do you speak English?"
That person says: "No, I can only speak Chinese."
I say: "That's OK, I can speak a little Chinese."
I ask him how to get to the train station, and he tells me.
I say: "Thank you!" He smiles and says: "You're welcome!"
On Saturday morning I did the laundry at home.
Because I went out to exercise every day this week, there were a lot of clothes to wash.
Our washing machine is small — one load takes an hour.
While the clothes were washing, I read a book next to it and drank a cup of tea.
An hour later, all the clothes were washed.
It didn't rain today, so the clothes were ready very quickly.
Tomorrow at work I can wear clean white clothes.
Last night my friend and I went out for hotpot — it was my first time eating it.
The restaurant was crowded and very hot.
On the table there were lamb, fish, and noodles.
My friend told me, "The meat is ready quickly in the pot — don't wait too long."
I ate a piece of lamb — it was so delicious, but also really spicy!
I drank a lot of water, and my eyes even turned red.
I said to my friend, "Next time I want to come again!"
Tomorrow is my mom's birthday, and I want to give her a gift.
I didn't know what to buy, so I asked my older sister.
My sister said: "Mom drinks tea every morning — why not give her some good tea?"
I went to a shop and bought tea, and I also bought a pretty piece of clothing.
When Mom saw the gifts, she was overjoyed.
She said: "The tea is lovely, but the clothes are a bit big."
I laughed: "No problem — next year I'll give you another one!"
My older brother lives in Shanghai, and today he is coming to Beijing.
I got up at six in the morning and took a taxi to the airport.
There were a lot of cars on the road, so we drove very slowly.
I got to the airport at nine, but my brother's plane had not arrived yet.
I bought a cup of coffee and sat there waiting for him.
At ten thirty my brother came out; he smiled and said, "Little brother, I missed you so much!"
In the morning, I go out and see grandpa at the doorway.
Grandpa says, "Morning! Morning to you too!"
I go to school, and on the way I see my friend Xiaomei.
Xiaomei says, "Good morning! Let's eat lunch together at noon, OK?"
I say, "Sure! See you at noon!"
At noon, Xiaomei and I eat lunch together, and we say, "See you tonight!"
In the evening, our whole family watches TV for a little while.
Mom says: "It's getting late, let's go to sleep."
Younger brother is tired, and goes back to his room first.
I say to him: "Good night, little brother!"
Older sister is going to sleep too, and she says: "Good night, see you tomorrow!"
I'm tired too, so I go back to my own room and say: "Good night!"
Last spring, mom started growing flowers at home.
She put a lot of flowerpots on the balcony, all different colors.
Every morning, she waters the flowers and even talks to them.
I asked her: "Can the flowers understand what you say?"
She smiled and said: "Maybe not, but it makes me happy."
In summer, the flowers on the balcony all bloomed — especially pretty.
Now every time I go home, I go look at those flowers on the balcony first.
My hair is too long — I want to get a haircut.
The barbershop isn't far from home — it's only a five-minute walk.
The barber asked me: "Would you like it cut shorter, or kept a bit longer?"
I said: "Cut it shorter, because summer is too hot."
After half an hour, my new hairstyle looked great.
After finishing the haircut, I looked in the mirror and felt more handsome.
The haircut only cost fifty kuai — I think that's cheap.
The New Year is almost here, and everyone is very happy.
Every New Year, I go home to visit my mom and dad.
This year I bought them tea and clothes, and also some fruit.
Mom made lots of delicious dishes, and we all ate happily.
Dad said to me: "Happy New Year — may your work go well and your health be good!"
I said: "Happy New Year to you too! I hope you're happy every single day!"
At New Year, being together with my mom and dad is when I feel happiest.
I'm at the station, and I can't read that character.
I saw a teacher and said, "Teacher, please help me look at this character."
The teacher looked at it and said, "No problem — this is the train to Beijing."
I said, "But I don't know where the train is — could you help me find it?"
The teacher smiled and said, "No problem, I'll take you there."
She led me to find the train, and I said, "Thank you — you really helped me."
Yesterday morning my friend got sick and couldn't get out of bed.
She called me and asked me to help her.
I went to the shop and bought her medicine and fruit.
I also made her noodles and eggs.
My friend took the medicine, rested for a day, and is now much better.
She smiled and said to me, "Thank you!" I feel that helping others is a real joy.
On Saturday afternoon, I wanted to go read at the library, but I didn't know the way.
On the road, I saw a classmate, and asked her: "Excuse me, how do I get to the library?"
She said: "Walk straight ahead, pass the park, turn right, and you're there."
I walked ahead, but I went the wrong way — what I saw wasn't the park, it was a store.
I called her and said: "I went the wrong way, I'm at the store, how do I get to the library?"
She said: "Right next to the store is the park — walk ahead a little more, turn right, and you're there."
I found the park, turned right, and quickly saw the library — I found a very interesting book and sat down to read.
I'm studying Chinese in China, but I still don't know the names of a lot of things.
Today, my friend and I are in the classroom, and there's an apple on the table.
I ask my friend: "How do you say this in Chinese?"
My friend says: "This is called píngguǒ (apple)."
I see a cup this time, and ask her too: "What about this one?"
She said, "That's a cup — you've learned two new things today!"
On Sunday, older brother wanted to ride his bike to the park, and I wanted to go too.
I asked him: "Is the park far or not far from our house?"
Older brother said: "Not far, but I don't know exactly how far either."
We asked dad, and he said: "The park isn't far from here — ten minutes by bike and you're there."
We were happy, and right away got on our bikes and went out.
After ten minutes of riding, we really did reach the park, and older brother laughed and said: "See, it's not far at all!"
My older sister is going to make a birthday cake and asks me to go help her.
I say: "Sorry, I don't know how to make cakes, and I don't know how to cook either."
My sister says: "It's fine if you don't know how — but you can't just sit there, come with me to the supermarket to buy things."
When we get to the supermarket, we buy eggs, milk, and some fruit.
After we get home, my sister makes the cake while I watch beside her, and I learn to do a little of it too.
In the evening, we eat the cake we made together.
In the afternoon, a student asked me for directions at the school gate.
He said, "Excuse me, where is the library?"
I don't know where the library is — I'm also a new student.
I told him, "You can ask Teacher Li — she knows."
The student said, "Thank you — I'll go ask her."
Afterward, he found Teacher Li, and she told him where the library was.
On Saturday afternoon, my friend and I were meeting at the bus stop to go watch a movie together.
At three o'clock, I arrived at the bus stop first, but I didn't see my friend.
I called her and said: "I've arrived, where are you?"
She said: "Sorry, I'll be there soon, wait a little longer."
Ten minutes later, I called her again and asked: "Have you arrived yet?"
She laughed and said: "I've arrived too, I'm at the bus stop entrance!"
I saw her, and we went into the cinema together and sat down to watch the movie.
Every Saturday I go play basketball.
We play from nine to eleven.
After the game, everyone drinks cola and eats watermelon together.
I work in Beijing and mom is in Shanghai; I miss her a lot.
In the evening I call mom and say: "Mom, I miss you."
Mom says: "I miss you too. What do you want to eat? I'll make it for you."
I say: "I want to eat noodles, but I'm not home."
Mom says: "Next month when you come home, I'll make you noodles."
I smile, but I still miss her a lot — I know she misses me the same way.
I go to the shop to buy fruit and want to buy apples, but apples aren't cheap.
The clerk asks me: "What do you want?"
I see a big watermelon and say: "I want this one!"
The clerk says: "This one is too big, that one is a bit smaller."
I say: "OK, then I'll take that one."
The clerk smiled and said, "Alright — that watermelon is yours."
Today, my friend Daming comes to my home to play.
I see him, feel glad, and say: "You're here, come on in!"
We eat cake together, and watch TV together.
In the evening, Daming is about to go home, and we talk at the doorway.
Mom asks me: "Were you happy today?"
Daming says: "Next time, let's play soccer together."
I'm afraid of dogs. Every time I see a dog, I get nervous right away.
Today, my friend and I are walking in the park, and see a little dog.
I'm very scared, and stand behind my friend.
Friend says: "Don't be afraid, this dog knows me, it's nice."
I slowly walk over to where the little dog is.
The little dog runs over and sits beside me.
Today I'm very busy, busy from morning until evening.
After work, I take the bus home.
After I get home, I sit on the sofa and say: "I'm tired."
Mom asks me: "Were you very busy today?"
I say: "Yes, I'm so tired, I want to rest a bit."
After I finish talking, I sleep on the sofa for a little while.
Our classroom isn't big, but it's very clean.
There are twenty desks and twenty chairs in the classroom.
The blackboard is at the front of the classroom, and the teacher stands in front of it.
My eyes aren't very good, so I like to sit in front.
When class is over, my classmates like to talk, and they also like to laugh.
I like my classroom and classmates very much.
On Sunday, I went to my friend's house to eat.
My friend made fish, and also noodles.
I first ate a piece of fish, and my friend asked me: "How is it?"
I then ate the noodles, and thought they were a little spicy.
My friend asked: "Are the noodles good?"
I said: "The noodles are so-so — the fish is better."
Today, I have a headache, so I sit in a chair to rest.
Friend sees me, and asks: "What's wrong?"
I say: "It's nothing, I'll be fine after resting a bit."
In the evening, my friend calls me and says: "Sorry, I forgot today is your birthday."
I say: "It's fine, thanks for calling me."
While eating, milk spills on the table, and I get anxious.
Mom says: "It's fine, just wipe it clean and it'll be okay."
In the afternoon, I'm going to the cinema to watch a movie with my friend.
Traffic on the way was slow, I got anxious, and by the time I ran to the cinema I was already late.
I say to my friend: "Sorry, I'm late."
My friend smiles and says: "It's okay, the movie hasn't started yet."
Afterward, at school I forgot to bring my classmate's book.
My classmate said, "It's nothing — just bring it tomorrow." I said, "Thank you."
This evening my wife and I went to a restaurant for dinner.
The waiter asked: "Would you like lamb or fish?"
I wanted lamb, but my wife said: "Lamb is too expensive!"
The fish was twenty kuai and the lamb was forty — the fish was cheaper than the lamb.
I said: "Lamb may be expensive, but it's really delicious."
My wife laughed: "Fine, let's order both dishes!"
That day, both the lamb and the fish were absolutely delicious.
Mom asked me, "Where did you see it?"
I said, "I remember I put it on the table."
Mom said, "It's not on the left side of the table — look on the right side."
I looked on the right side too, but still didn't find it.
Later, I found the phone under the sofa.
Mom smiled and said, "Next time put it away properly — don't just put it anywhere."
In the evening, a few friends and I have dinner together and talk a lot.
It's getting late, so I say: "Let's go!"
My friend says: "OK, let's go — we'll take the bus."
We walk to the doorway, but Xiao Wang is still sitting there and hasn't gotten up.
I say: "Xiao Wang, let's go — stop talking!"
Xiao Wang laughs and says: "OK, OK, let's go!"
At noon, my coworker and I went to have lunch together.
Next to the company there's a small restaurant, and its dishes are famous.
My coworker asked me: "Would you like to eat rice or noodles?"
I said: "Either is fine, I'm not picky about food."
We ordered two dishes, and also asked for a bowl of soup.
While eating, we chatted a bit about the company's new project.
This lunch was simple, but we were both very happy.
On Saturday, my friend and I went to the store to buy some things.
I saw a book and said, "I want to buy this book."
The clerk smiled and said, "For books you should say 'yì běn,' not 'yí gè.'"
This time, I bought a cup of coffee and a piece of cake.
My friend said, "Now you've got it!"
I still wanted to buy a piece of clothing, but I was running low on money.
Every morning, I drink a cup of milk and eat an egg.
Mom says milk and eggs are very good for your health.
Before, I didn't like drinking milk — I thought it didn't taste good.
Now I drink it every day — I'm already used to it.
Eggs can be eaten boiled, or made into egg soup.
After drinking milk and eating eggs, I feel full of energy.
Last year my health wasn't very good, and I didn't like exercising either.
The doctor told me, "Running is good for your health — you should exercise more."
Now I get up at six every morning and go running in the park next to my home.
At the beginning, I would get tired after running for just ten minutes.
Now I can run for thirty minutes, and I also run faster than before.
The park is beautiful in the morning — birds are singing, and there are many people out running.
Exercise is making my health better day by day.
In the evening, my coworker called me.
He said, "Sorry, it's very late now."
I said, "It's fine — I haven't gone to sleep yet."
He said, "Can you come to the office tomorrow? We have a lot to get done."
I said, "No problem — I'll go tomorrow morning."
Afterward, we got through all of it together.
At noon, my classmate and I went to a restaurant to eat noodles.
The server asked how many bowls we wanted; I said two bowls.
The noodles were delicious, and I finished mine in no time.
I was still hungry, and said to the server: "One more bowl!"
After I finished that bowl, my classmate said: "You're eating so much today!"
I said: "It's so delicious! One more bowl, please — is that okay?"
At noon my classmate and I go to a restaurant to eat.
The server asks us: "What would you like to eat?"
I ordered fish, and my classmate ordered lamb and rice.
We also ordered two cups of tea.
The food came quickly, and the fish was really delicious.
After finishing the meal, we went right back to school for class.
This restaurant's food is tasty and cheap; we want to come again next time.
My husband goes to play football every Sunday.
This Sunday, he asked me to come and watch too.
The weather was great; they played behind the school, and many people were watching.
My husband ran very fast and kicked in two goals.
Everyone laughed and said, "That was great!"
On the way home he was very tired, but extremely happy.
He asked me, "Will you come again next week?" I said, "Yes, I will!"
Next Wednesday I have a Chinese exam.
There are a lot of questions, so I study for two hours every evening.
When there are questions I don't understand, I go and ask my teacher.
My teacher told me: "You've already learned it very well."
But all this studying has worn me out — I really want to sleep.
Last night I said to my books: "See you tomorrow!"
I hope the exam comes soon — once it's over, I'm going to sleep for ten hours!
At dinner in the evening, my son was looking at his phone.
I said: "Put the phone down and eat — the food is getting cold."
He said: "Just a moment, my friend is waiting for me."
I told him that looking at a phone too long every day makes your eyes tired.
After he heard that, he stopped looking at his phone.
That evening we talked a lot, and I felt really happy.
I think that from now on, none of us should look at a phone during meals.
Grandpa reads the newspaper every morning.
He drinks tea while reading the newspaper.
Today's newspaper says it will rain tomorrow.
Grandpa told me, "Don't forget to bring an umbrella tomorrow."
I thanked grandpa, and said that his reading the newspaper every day is really good.
Grandpa smiled and said, "Reading the newspaper lets you know about many things."
My friend calls me and says he wants to give me a new phone.
I say: "Really? How come you have two phones?"
He says: "This one is my sister's — she bought a new one and doesn't want this one anymore."
I still don't quite get it, so I ask: "Can you really give it to me?"
He smiles and says: "Really, I'll bring it to you tomorrow."
Afterward, he really did bring the phone and gave it to me — I smile and say: "Thank you!"
Yesterday my little sister and I went to the shop to buy clothes.
I saw a red skirt — it was really pretty.
But it was a bit expensive — three hundred kuai.
My sister said: "Red looks best on you — buy it!"
I thought about it for a moment, and then I bought it.
Today I wore my new skirt to a friend's house, and everyone said: "So pretty!"
My sister laughed and said: "Next time buy one for me too!"
This morning I got up late — it was already ten past eight.
Work starts at nine at my company, but the way there is long.
I left home without eating breakfast.
There were a lot of people on the bus, and it was moving very slowly too.
I got to the company at nine twenty — twenty minutes late.
I said to everyone, "Sorry, I'm late!"
Starting tomorrow, I'm going to go to bed a bit earlier and get up a bit earlier.
In the afternoon, Xiaomei and Xiao Wang read books in the library.
After reading for an hour, Xiaomei said: "I'm going to drink some water, see you in a bit."
Five minutes later, she came back, and the two of them sat down to read again.
It got dark, and Xiao Wang was about to leave. He said: "I'm heading out first, let's eat together tonight, see you later!"
While eating dinner in the evening, Xiao Wang asked: "Are you still coming to the library tomorrow?"
Xiaomei said: "Yes, let's meet at eight at the door, see you tomorrow!"
I bought a book for my mom, and I want to send it to her by courier.
The delivery company is next to the supermarket, not too far from my home.
The staff member asked me: "Where would you like to send it to?"
I said: "Send it to Beijing — my mom lives there."
She said because the item isn't heavy, it only costs twenty kuai.
I paid, and the staff member gave me a receipt slip.
She said in three days my mom would be able to receive the package.
Last night I felt really unwell — maybe I was getting sick.
This morning I didn't go to work; I went to the hospital.
I said, "I have a headache, and I've got a fever too."
The doctor gave me some medicine and told me to drink more water and get more rest.
I slept for a whole day, and now I feel much better.
On Saturday evening, my friends and I went out singing together.
My friend Xiao Wang sings extremely well; everyone loves listening to him.
Although I don't sing well, I sing very happily.
When the singing was done, everyone began to dance.
Xiao Wang dances better than I do, so I watched him and slowly learned.
By the time we went home it was already twelve o'clock, but everyone was very happy.
When I got up this morning, I saw it was snowing outside.
The snow was heavy — the roads were all white, and it was very beautiful.
The weather was very cold, so I put on a lot of clothes.
The children were playing in the snow outside, laughing happily.
My friend and I made a big snowman.
In the evening it was still snowing, and I stayed home drinking hot tea and reading.
I think snowy weather is really lovely.
Grandpa calls me; he talks very fast, and I can't understand him.
I say: "Grandpa, please speak a little slower."
Grandpa speaks slowly, but I still hadn't understood the name he said.
I say: "Grandpa, please say it again."
Grandpa said it again, and I understood: he's coming to my house.
I tell my family right away: "Grandpa is coming!"
I couldn't swim before, but my husband swims very well.
He said to me, "Swimming is good for your health — come with me!"
Last month we started going swimming twice every week.
At the beginning, I got tired after swimming for just one minute.
Now I can already swim for a long time.
Yesterday my husband watched me swim, and he said with a smile, "You swim really well!"
I think swimming is the happiest sport of all.
My company is far from home, so I take the bus to work every day.
It was raining this morning, and a lot of people were waiting for the bus at the stop.
The bus came, and everyone got on.
There were no seats on the bus, so I stood for twenty minutes.
A student said to me, "I'm getting off soon — take my seat."
I said, "Thank you!" The rain was heavy, but I felt happy.
Saturday afternoon, I'm home alone, and I miss my friend a lot.
My friend calls me and says: "Tomorrow I'll come see you — neither of us has work!"
I say: "That's great! I'll wait for you."
On Sunday, my friend comes, and we go eat together happily.
After finishing the meal, my friend says: "Next month I'll come again."
I say with a smile: "That's great, I'll wait for you to come again!"
My home is very close to the library — it's only a ten-minute walk.
Every Saturday morning I go there to read.
There are lots of people in the library, but nobody talks.
Yesterday I borrowed three books, and they're all really interesting.
My favorite is a book about coffee.
After finishing my book, I had a cup of coffee next to the library.
Books and coffee — that's my happiest kind of Saturday.
At noon, my friend and I walked into a restaurant, and the server gave us a menu.
I took a look at the menu, and asked the server: "What dishes do you have?"
The server said: "We have fish, and also lamb."
I wanted to order fish, but the server said the lamb was even better.
My friend also said: "Let's just order the lamb!"
So we ordered lamb and rice.
Next to my home there is a man who sells watermelons; he comes every morning.
His watermelons are big — fifteen yuan each.
When the weather is hot, he sells from eight in the morning until seven at night.
Yesterday I bought a big watermelon, and he said: "This one is the best — you'll like it."
I asked him whether he was tired. He said: "A little tired, but my child has to go to school."
After I got home, my child and I ate the watermelon together — it was really good.
This morning I saw him again — he was still there selling watermelons.
Today I worked all day, and I felt very tired.
In the evening I went home, and I didn't want to do anything.
Mom saw that I was very tired, and said, "If you're tired, you should rest a bit."
I listened to mom's words, and rested on the bed for a bit.
After resting for twenty minutes, I felt much better.
Once you're tired, rest a bit — then your body will be fine.
Today, I want to buy a watermelon.
I went to the store and saw someone selling big watermelons.
I ask him: "How much is this watermelon?"
He says: "Thirty kuai." I think it's too expensive.
I say: "Too expensive! Can it be a little cheaper?"
He smiles and says: "OK, twenty-five kuai, how about that?"
I paid and went home. The watermelon was so good I ate three slices on my own.
Next month my wife and I want to travel to Beijing.
This is our travel plan: we intend to spend a week having fun.
I bought the plane tickets on my phone; they were not too expensive.
We also found a hotel that is very close to the train station.
My wife says Beijing has lots of tasty food, and she wants to try it all.
I hope the weather is sunny so we can have a very happy time.
On Saturday afternoon I go to my friend's home as a guest.
I bought some apples and a watermelon to give him.
My friend's mom cooked a lot of delicious dishes.
We ate together and talked a lot.
The kitten at his home is very pretty; I like it a lot.
At nine in the evening I went home; today I had a really great time.
In the afternoon, a friend comes over to hang out with me.
I'm cooking, so I say: "Wait a moment, I'll come as soon as I'm done."
After a little while, a coworker calls.
I say: "Wait a moment, I'm busy."
In the evening, I'm about to go out when my friend calls out to me.
He says: "Wait a moment, let's go together."
I smile and say: "OK, I'll wait for you."
Yesterday at noon, my friend and I went to a restaurant and ate a lot of dishes.
When we finished eating, I said to the waiter: "Waiter, the bill, please!"
The waiter said: "That's ninety-eight kuai in total."
My friend wanted to pay, and I wanted to pay too.
I said: "Last time you paid — this time it's on me!"
My friend laughed and said: "Alright, next time it's my treat!"
When you eat with a good friend, even paying the bill feels happy.
Every morning I take the bus to work.
Today is overcast, and there are a lot of people waiting for the bus.
I waited for thirty minutes, and the bus still hadn't come.
A girl next to me asked, "Are you waiting for the route 3 bus too?"
We chatted together, and the waiting time passed quickly.
When the bus came, everyone was very happy.
Although I waited a long time, I made a new friend.
My husband has an old watch that his father gave him.
The watch runs five minutes slow every day.
So every day he asks me: "What time is it now?"
Yesterday morning his watch said seven o'clock, but it was actually already ten past seven.
By the time he got to the office, everyone had already started working.
I said to him: "Buy a new watch — they're not expensive."
He smiled and said: "No! This is Dad's watch. Starting tomorrow, I'll just get up a little earlier!"
Every evening, I watch the weather forecast.
Yesterday the TV said, "Tomorrow there will be rain, and it will be very cold."
This morning when I left home, the sky was overcast, so I put on a lot of clothes.
But at noon it didn't rain — the sky turned sunny, and it was even hot!
I was wearing too much; after walking just a little I was so hot I didn't even want to talk.
I smiled and thought: sometimes the weather forecast can be wrong too.
Tomorrow I will still watch the weather forecast, but I will also take a look at the sky myself!
On Saturday the weather is great.
My girlfriend and I go to the park together.
There are lots of people in the park — some are jogging, some are singing.
We sit under a tree, drinking tea and chatting.
Time passes so quickly — we spend the whole afternoon having fun.
Today, a new coworker came to the company.
Everyone smiles and says: "Welcome to our company!"
The new coworker says: "Thank you everyone, I'm happy to meet you all."
I say: "You're welcome, sit down, let's have tea together."
When it's time to get off work, the new coworker says to me: "The people at this company are really nice."
She smiles and says: "Thank you all, I really like this company!"
In the evening I call my friend and ask: "What are you doing?"
She says: "I'm making a cake right now — tomorrow is my mom's birthday."
I say: "That's so fun! Can I take a look?"
She said, "Give it a moment and it'll be ready — come and have some!"
I say: "Great, I'll head over right now — I want to help you too."
By the time I arrive, the cake is already done, and we wait together for mom to come home.
My friend and I are eating at a restaurant, and there are a lot of people inside — it's very noisy.
My friend is talking to me, but it's too noisy, and I don't hear him clearly.
I ask him: "What did you say?"
My friend says it again, but I still don't hear it clearly.
We walk outside the restaurant, where there aren't as many people.
My friend says it again, and this time I hear it clearly: "We're going to watch a movie tomorrow."
At noon, my classmate looks at my food and says: "You're too picky about food!"
I don't know what that means, so I ask her: "What does 'tiāoshí' mean?"
She says: "'Tiāoshí' means you don't eat this, and you don't eat that either."
I say: "I'm not picky, I just don't like fish."
She smiles and says: "You're really interesting."
I say: "What do you mean? Are you saying I'm bad?"
She says: "No, I mean you're really interesting."
Tomorrow is my friend's birthday, and in the evening we are all going to have dinner together.
Tonight I asked my husband, "What should I wear tomorrow?"
He said, "Wear that red one — you look the most beautiful in red."
I said, "I bought that one last year — isn't it too big now?"
My husband smiled and said, "It's not too big — you look good in anything."
I was very happy and said, "Okay, I'll wear it tomorrow!"
He said, "Stop thinking about it and go to sleep — tomorrow you will be the most beautiful one there!"
I call my friend and ask: "When shall we meet?"
She says: "Three o'clock in the afternoon, at the park."
In the afternoon, I arrive at the park, but I don't see her, so I call and ask: "Where are you? When will you get here?"
She says: "Sorry, I'll be there right away, wait a moment."
Afterward, she comes running over and says: "I'm here, I'm here, let's go!"
A lot of friends ask me: "Why do you study Chinese?"
Three years ago I traveled to China for the first time.
In Beijing I wanted to ask for directions, but I couldn't speak Chinese.
Right then I thought: I'm going to learn Chinese.
Now I have already studied for two years, and I can talk with Chinese friends.
Learning Chinese is slow, but I find it very interesting.
I hope to go to China again next year and use Chinese to buy things and ask for directions.
My husband gets up at six every day and goes to work.
I'm the wife, and I cook at home.
In the evening, when my husband comes home, we eat together.
He likes to eat fish and I like to eat vegetables, so the dishes we make are different.
On weekends, we go for a walk in the park together, and we also watch movies together.
We're both busy with work, but we're both happy.
On the weekend, I help mom cook at home, and she's happy.
When we finish, mom smiles and says: "Thank you!" I say: "You're welcome."
After we finish eating, my brother can't do his homework, so I sit down to help him.
My brother is happy and says: "Thanks, sis!" I say: "No worries, we're family."
In the evening, a classmate calls and says: "Thank you for helping me today."
I said, "No need to thank me — see you tomorrow!"
This morning, my alarm clock didn't ring, and I got up half an hour late.
I immediately got out of bed, but I couldn't find my key, and I was extremely anxious.
When I went out, it was raining hard outside, and I hadn't brought an umbrella.
I ran to the bus stop, but the bus had already driven off.
I had no choice but to take a taxi to the office, but there were a lot of cars on the road, and we moved very slowly.
When I arrived at the office, I discovered that today's meeting time had changed, and actually I didn't need to worry at all.
My colleagues saw that I was both tired and anxious, and they all laughed.
Although this day was stressful, in the end everything went smoothly.
Last night, my friend and I watched a soccer match together.
Both teams played well, and the score stayed close the whole time.
Not long after the match started, one team scored a goal, and everyone got very excited.
In the last five minutes, the score was still tied, and everyone was very tense.
Right when the match was about to end, a player suddenly scored a goal.
The whole stadium was extremely excited, shouting loudly.
That match was really interesting — I still remember it to this day.
Last year on my birthday I was working in another city, staying alone in a hotel.
It rained all day; I was both tired and homesick, and I was sure this birthday was going to be really dull.
At eight in the evening I sat alone in my room eating instant noodles; the room was extremely quiet.
Suddenly a few colleagues called me and told me to come downstairs right away.
When I came down, I saw them standing in the doorway holding a small cake.
The cake was not big and it was not very sweet, but it was the best cake I have ever eaten.
Laughing, they said: "How could we ever forget your birthday?"
That night, although I was far from home, I was not sad at all — it was the most unforgettable birthday I have ever had.
I had a headache and a bit of a fever, so I went to the pharmacy to buy medicine.
The clerk at the pharmacy asked me: "Where does it hurt?"
I said: "I have a headache and a fever — I feel awful."
The clerk handed me a box of medicine and said: "Take it three times a day, two pills each time."
I asked: "How much is this?" She said: "Fifteen kuai."
I paid, said thank you, and went home.
After taking the medicine for two days, my head didn't hurt anymore, and the fever was gone too.
I called my mom, and she said, "Glad you're better — just remember to drink plenty of water."
On Saturday, my son and I went to the zoo together.
We first looked at the elephant, and my son said the elephant's nose was really long.
Then we went to see the panda, which was eating bamboo — very cute.
My son liked the tiger the most; he said the tiger ran very fast, like the wind.
At noon, we ate lunch at a restaurant there and rested for a while.
In the afternoon, we saw many more birds and fish, and my son took quite a few photos.
Before it got dark, we finally went home, and my son said this was his happiest day.
Last Saturday, I attended a Chinese friend's wedding for the first time.
Because I didn't know what to wear, I asked a coworker beforehand.
She told me: "You'd better not wear black clothes, and you also need to prepare the red envelope in advance."
On the day of the wedding, the bride and groom were dressed beautifully, and a lot of guests came too.
As soon as the wedding started, the groom spoke while shedding tears, and everyone at the scene laughed.
Although I didn't understand a lot of the customs, the friends beside me warmly explained them to me.
At the wedding banquet in the evening, everyone toasted and sang together, and the atmosphere got livelier and livelier.
This wedding helped me understand Chinese culture better, and made me like this country even more.
Yesterday afternoon, my friend and I went out to buy some things.
I was walking while looking at my phone, and didn't watch the traffic light.
Suddenly, a bicycle came riding very fast, very close to me.
I quickly stepped to the side, and the bicycle rode past.
My heart was pounding, but nothing had happened.
My friend said again: "When you walk, watch out for cars — don't look at your phone."
Since then, I never look at my phone while walking again.
I've lived in Beijing for two years now, and I've found the four seasons here are all very different.
In spring, the flowers in the parks all bloom, but the wind is a bit strong.
Summer is especially hot; in the evenings people like to sit outside eating and chatting.
Autumn is Beijing's best season — the sky is blue, and it's neither cold nor hot.
In autumn, many people go to the parks to see the leaves that have turned red.
Winter is very cold; it's often windy, and sometimes it even snows.
Last winter I saw snow for the first time and was as happy as a child.
If you want to visit Beijing, let me tell you: autumn is the best time to come!
This weekend, I went to the library and worked as a volunteer once.
After signing up, the staff member arranged for me to organize bookshelves.
At first I thought this job was simple, but there were so many books, and they were arranged so messily.
According to the books' titles, I put them back one by one to their original positions.
During the break, an elderly person couldn't find a book she wanted to read, so I helped her find it.
She thanked me happily several times, and I felt happy in my heart too.
Although organizing bookshelves was tiring work, I felt it was very meaningful to be able to help others.
If I have the chance in the future, I still want to go be a volunteer again.
Saturday afternoon, a friend treated me to a movie, and we bought two tickets.
The movie was pretty good when it started, but after half an hour, I found it really boring.
My friend said too: "This movie is so boring, so dull, I'm about to fall asleep."
I glanced at my watch — only forty minutes had passed. I thought to myself: there's still a whole hour left.
The movie wasn't even over yet, and we walked out of the cinema together.
The weather outside was nice, so we went for a walk in a nearby park.
We sat in the park for a long time, chatting about all kinds of other things.
I love reading, but books are too expensive, so I often go to the library to borrow them.
On Saturday morning, I rode my bike to the library next to the school.
The book I wanted to borrow is very famous, but I searched for ages and still couldn't find it.
I asked the staff member: "Excuse me, where is that book?"
She said: "That book has been borrowed by someone; it won't be back until next Monday."
I first borrowed two other books, then wrote my name on the library card.
The staff member told me a book can be borrowed for one month, and it must be returned on time.
Next Monday I'll go one more time — I hope I can get that famous book.
Next Monday, I'm going to Shanghai on a business trip with my manager.
It's my first business trip, so I feel both excited and a little worried.
On Sunday evening, I put my clothes and my computer into the suitcase.
At six o'clock the next morning, we took a taxi to the airport.
On the plane, the manager told me: "When we arrive in Shanghai, we'll go to the hotel first, then go meet the clients."
In the afternoon we had a three-hour meeting, and the clients were very satisfied with us.
In the evening, the manager treated me to Shanghai's most famous dishes.
The business trip ended quickly; I feel I learned a lot — it was really great!
I just arrived in China, and I need to buy a SIM card.
I went to a shop, and saw a lot of people there buying SIM cards.
The staff member said: "Please let me see your passport."
I handed him my passport, and he quickly gave me a SIM card and a new number.
I asked: "How much is it per month?"
He said: "Not expensive — fifty yuan a month, and you can make calls and send messages."
I was satisfied — I finally had a Chinese phone number.
Now I can use my Chinese number to call my family.
My friend and I went to a store to buy clothes, and I saw a shirt whose color looked great.
I asked the clerk: "Can I try it on?"
The clerk said: "Of course, the mirror is right beside you."
I put on the shirt, looked at myself in the mirror, and felt it was a bit too big.
I asked the clerk: "Do you have a smaller size?"
The clerk brought me another one, and I put it on and tried it out.
This time it wasn't too big or too small — it fit just right.
I paid, carried the shirt out of the store, and my friend was still nearby trying on a skirt.
Last Saturday morning my colleague Xiao Li called me, and his voice sounded strange.
He said he had fallen ill and had been running a fever since last night; he was home alone and hadn't eaten a thing.
I was a bit worried, so I went straight to the supermarket, bought fruit and noodles, and rode my bike over to his place.
When I got there, I found the room was cold, and the medicine he had bought the day before was still sitting on the table.
First I tidied the room up a bit, then I made him a bowl of hot noodles.
Eating his noodles, he smiled and said: "Thank you — you really are my best friend."
In the afternoon I went with him to the hospital for a check-up; the doctor said it was nothing serious and a few days' good rest would be enough.
He is well again now, and he says that next time I get sick he will definitely take good care of me too.
I have a friend who lives in America; we haven't seen each other in a long time.
Last night, I turned on my computer and chatted with him online.
He asked me how I've been recently, and whether work has been busy.
I told him that I've changed to a new job, and also moved to a new home.
He said he plans to travel to China next year, and wants to come see me.
I was happy to hear this, and immediately said, great, welcome!
We chatted for more than two hours, but we still felt the time was too short.
Today is my friend's birthday, and in the evening a few of us went to a restaurant together.
After everyone sat down, the clerk brought a glass of beer for each person.
My friend picked up their glass, smiling, and said: "Thanks everyone for coming."
Everyone else picked up their glasses too, and said together: "Happy birthday, and good health!"
After that, everyone said together, "Cheers!" and then everyone drank a glass of beer.
A while into the meal my friend raised his glass again, and everyone joined in: "Ganbei!"
We ate for a long time and drank a lot of beer, and finally walked out of the restaurant together.
Last year I made a Chinese friend named Xiaolong.
He is especially kind to me and often helps me practice Chinese.
When we eat together, he teaches me how to use chopsticks.
At first I was terrible at it, and everyone laughed.
Now I can not only use chopsticks, but also cook a few Chinese dishes.
It's so good to have friends!
I want to find a new job; right now I have two opportunities.
One job is close to home; it doesn't pay much, but it's relaxed and easy.
There's also a job in another city that pays a bit more, but I would need to travel for business often.
Mom thinks the higher-paying job is better, since later I could buy a house.
But I don't want to leave my family and friends.
I thought about it for many days, and finally chose the job close to home.
Although it doesn't pay much, I feel relaxed every day, and also happy.
I think this decision was the right one.
The weather was great on Saturday, so three coworkers and I went mountain climbing.
At eight in the morning we met at the foot of the mountain, and everyone brought water and bread.
At first I climbed fast, but later my legs got more and more tired.
A coworker said to me, "Don't rush — let's climb slowly."
At twelve noon, we finally reached the top of the mountain.
Looking down from the mountain, the buildings in the city looked tiny — it was incredibly beautiful.
We ate our bread at the top and rested for half an hour.
Although my legs ached after I got home, I still want to climb again next month.
Next Friday my friend has a running race, and he practices in the park every day.
On the day of the race, the weather was hot, and I went to the park too to watch him run.
The race began, and lots of people stood by the side watching.
I shouted loudly too: "Jiāyóu! You can do it!"
My friend ran very fast, and soon got to the front.
After the race ended, he was happy and said with a smile: "Thanks — cheering me on really worked!"
At noon I treated him to lunch, and he said next time he wants me to come cheer him on again.
My friend Xiao Li had been job-hunting for a long time, and hadn't found one.
Last week, he went to interview at a company.
Yesterday, the company called and told him he could start work.
Xiao Li was so happy, he called me right away and told me the good news.
I said: "Congratulations, you finally found a job!"
In the evening, a few classmates treated him to a meal together, and everyone said to him: "Congratulations!"
Xiao Li raised his glass: "Thank you all — next one's on me."
I used to get up at seven thirty every morning, and I was always in a hurry.
I often looked for clothes while brushing my teeth, and sometimes I went out the door having forgotten to wash my face.
Starting last month, I made myself get up at six fifty.
Now I first brush my teeth and wash my face, then quietly eat breakfast and drink a cup of hot milk.
After finishing my meal, I even have time to watch the news for a while.
Now this has become my habit, and I'm never in a hurry in the morning any more.
Who knew that getting up forty minutes earlier would make my whole day different.
Tomorrow I have an exam, but I still haven't finished reviewing — I'm worried.
My friend said: "Don't worry, you've already worked so hard."
I said: "But I'm still nervous — I feel like I won't do well."
My friend said: "Relax — you study every day, it'll definitely be fine."
When exam day came, the questions weren't hard, and I could answer them all.
After the exam, I called my friend and said: "It's great, everything's fine!"
My friend laughed and said, "See? I told you so."
Next month I plan to travel abroad, so this morning I went to the bank to exchange money.
The bank was especially crowded; after taking a number, I waited forty minutes before I got to see a staff member.
She asked me: "Hello, how much money would you like to exchange?"
I said: "I'd like to exchange five thousand yuan for US dollars."
She asked me to show her my passport, then had me write my name.
A dozen or so minutes later, I had a little over seven hundred US dollars in hand.
Walking out of the bank, I thought to myself: the money is all exchanged — now I'm just waiting for my trip!
I work at a company, sitting eight or nine hours a day, and lately I've been feeling especially tired all the time.
Last week I had a check-up at the hospital; the doctor said I was too heavy and should exercise more.
I decided to get up at six thirty every morning and go jogging in the park near my home.
After my first run, my legs ached so much I didn't want to walk, but I still went every day.
On weekends I often go hiking with friends, or we ride bikes.
While hiking, we climb and chat at the same time — we get exercise and have a great time.
A month later, exercising had already become a habit, and I was getting healthier and healthier.
Now I rarely catch colds, and I don't get as tired at work as I used to.
The night before last it rained heavily and I hadn't brought an umbrella; by the time I got home, my clothes were soaked.
Yesterday morning, as soon as I got up, my head hurt and I kept wanting to sleep.
I thought I might have caught a cold, so I took a little medicine, but by evening I had started running a fever.
This morning I took the day off work and went to the hospital to see a doctor.
The doctor examined me and said: "You have a cold, and you're running a fever of thirty-eight degrees."
He told me to take medicine for three days first, then rest well at home and drink plenty of water.
Now I've taken my medicine and I'm lying in bed, feeling much better than yesterday.
From now on, when it rains I'll definitely bring an umbrella — good health matters most!
Today was my first day at work, and I got up as early as six thirty.
When I arrived at the company, there wasn't a single person in the office.
At nine o'clock the manager introduced me to everyone, and my colleagues were all very warm.
A colleague surnamed Wang taught me how to use the company's computer.
At noon, she even treated me to noodles downstairs.
In the afternoon I attended my first meeting; there was a lot I couldn't understand, but I wrote it all down in my notebook.
On my way home in the evening, I was both tired and happy.
When my roommate and I first started living together, our relationship wasn't good at all.
She liked to go to sleep very late at night, whereas I was used to going to bed early and getting up early.
Because of this problem, we argued several times, and the atmosphere became more and more tense.
Later, we decided to sit down and have a proper talk, and each spoke our own thoughts.
We set a rule together: after eleven o'clock, no turning on lights, and no talking loudly either.
If a friend wanted to come over, we would let the other person know in advance.
Actually she's a really nice person — every time I got sick, she would buy medicine for me.
Now we have already become good friends, and I feel that understanding each other is really important.
Last weekend, I rode my bike to the park alone to have some fun.
On the way home, it got dark, and I found that I was lost.
My phone was out of battery too, so I couldn't check the map, and I was extremely anxious.
I asked an elderly man by the road: "Excuse me, how do I get to Zhongshan Road?"
He said warmly: "Keep walking straight ahead; when you reach the traffic light, walk to the right for ten minutes and you'll be there."
I soon found the way home, and my heart was finally at ease.
From now on, every time I go out, I will check the map carefully first.
Mid-Autumn Festival was coming, and all the shops were selling mooncakes.
My Chinese colleague told me that at Mid-Autumn Festival, people give mooncakes to family and friends.
I bought two boxes of mooncakes — one for my Chinese teacher, and one for the neighbor downstairs.
There are many kinds of mooncakes: some are sweet with fruit inside, and some even have egg inside.
When I gave the mooncakes to my teacher, she said with a smile, "You're becoming more and more like a Chinese person!"
The auntie downstairs was also very happy; the next day she gave us some apples.
My colleague said that giving mooncakes means: although we can't meet often, you are on my mind.
I think this custom is really lovely — next Mid-Autumn Festival I want to give mooncakes again.
Spring Festival was coming soon, so I decided to go home to see my parents.
Train tickets before Spring Festival are extremely hard to get; I searched online for three days before I finally got one.
That day the train station was packed; everyone was carrying lots of bags, with smiles on their faces.
The train ran for ten hours, and I kept watching the snow outside the whole way.
It was already evening when I got home; Mom had made a whole table of dishes and had also wrapped my favorite dumplings.
Dad looked at me and said, "A whole year without seeing you — you've gotten thinner. Eat more!"
After dinner we watched TV together and talked and talked, late into the night.
Although the journey home is long, spending Spring Festival with my family is better than anything.
Today is Xiaomei's birthday, and a few of us friends went to her home together.
After everyone sat down, we first sang her a song together, and once we finished singing, we all said together: "Happy birthday!"
Xiaomei said with a smile: "Thank you everyone, I'm very happy."
Then I took out the gift I had prepared, gave it to her, and said to her: "I wish you good health and smooth work!"
Xiaomei looked at the gift, very happy, and said: "Wonderful, thank you!"
While we were all eating cake together, Xiaomei said to us again: "I wish you all smooth work too!"
Xiaomei cut the cake for everyone, and the last piece went to her mom.
Last night I had a slight fever, and my head hurt a lot too.
This morning, I went to the hospital with a colleague to see a doctor.
The hospital was really crowded; we first registered on the first floor.
While registering, the lady asked me: "Where do you feel unwell?"
I said: "I have a fever; it's probably a cold."
The doctor examined me and said it was nothing serious, telling me to drink more water and get more rest.
After picking up the medicine, I went home to sleep, and now I feel much better.
This morning I was going to take the train to Shanghai, but I got up late.
Mom glanced at the time and shouted: "Hurry up, there's no time left!"
I quickly threw on my clothes, grabbed my bag, and ran straight outside.
As I left, I saw that the bus had already driven off.
I was anxious, so I had no choice but to take a taxi to the train station.
The taxi driver said: "Don't worry, we still have time."
By the time I got to the train station, the train was leaving in five minutes.
I made it onto the train, and only once I sat down did the panic settle.
Over the weekend a few of us friends were eating together, discussing where to go on Saturday.
Xiaomei said: "Let's go hiking, the weather's so nice."
Xiaozhang said: "I agree, hiking's good exercise too."
I said: "I think so too, we haven't gone out together in ages."
So we decided to meet at the park entrance at eight on Saturday morning.
Saturday morning, we all arrived at the park entrance and went hiking together.
When we got to the top, Xiaomei took out her phone and took a photo of all of us.
In the evening I ate at Xiaomei's home, and Xiaomei's mom made a lot of dishes.
We had been eating for a long time, and there was still a lot of food on the table.
Xiaomei's mom brought me another dish and said: "Eat a little more!"
I said: "Thank you, but I'm really full, I can't eat any more."
Xiaomei's mom said with a smile: "Have a little more, this dish is delicious."
Xiaomei said to her mom: "Mom, he's really full, don't make him eat any more."
Mom laughed and said: "OK, then I'll go get some fruit."
After class, I was hungry and thirsty, so I called a classmate.
I said: "I'm hungry — do you want to get food together?"
He said: "Sure, I'm hungry too — let's go to that restaurant."
We walked to the restaurant, looked at the menu, and ordered rice and a dish.
After a while, the clerk brought the dish over, and we started eating.
While eating, I said: "This is so good — I'm finally not hungry anymore."
After finishing the meal, I was still a bit thirsty, so I ordered another glass of water.
My best friend is moving to another city, and I feel really sad.
We've been good friends since elementary school, and we've had fun together for many years.
Mom saw that I wasn't happy and asked me what was wrong.
I said: "My good friend is moving away, and I'm really sad."
Mom said: "Don't be sad, you can still call each other and chat, and you'll definitely see each other from now on."
The day my friend left, we met at the station, and I gave her a photo.
In the photo, the two of us are standing at the park entrance, smiling happily.
She put the photo into her bag, said "goodbye" to me, and walked into the station.
Last Wednesday I went to a company for a job interview.
The evening before, I prepared a lot of questions and didn't go to sleep until very late.
In the morning I got up very early, because I didn't want to be late.
I wore a white shirt, hoping the manager would think I was serious.
The manager asked me: "Why do you want to come work at our company?"
I was a little nervous, but I answered every question carefully.
When the interview ended, the manager said with a smile: "Not bad. Go home and wait for our call."
Yesterday they really did call — next month I'll be starting work!
I walked into a store, just wanting to look around — I didn't want to buy anything.
The clerk saw me and said warmly: "Welcome! Do you need any help?"
I said: "No need, thanks — I'm just looking."
The clerk stayed at my elbow the whole time, moving from one item to the next.
I looked for a long time, but still didn't know what I wanted to buy.
Suddenly, I saw a cup that looked just like the broken one at my house.
I picked up the cup and asked the clerk how much it cost.
I paid, and once I got home, I put the new cup right next to the broken one.
I love eating Chinese food and have always wanted to learn how to cook it.
Last weekend, my Chinese friend invited me to her home and taught me to make tomato and egg stir-fry.
First we went to the supermarket and bought eggs and tomatoes.
My friend said, "This dish is easy, but don't forget to add the salt."
The first dish I made was too salty; my friend took one bite and laughed.
The second time I used a little less salt, and it turned out much better than the first.
That evening we ate and chatted at the same time — the time flew by.
Now I can make this dish, and next week I want to cook it for my mom.
On the street I suddenly ran into an old classmate — we hadn't seen each other in ages.
He was happy to see me too, and we just stood there on the street chatting.
I asked him: "How have you been? Are you still working at that company?"
He said: "I changed jobs — now I'm a manager at a small company."
I said: "You're still just as thin — you haven't changed a bit."
He laughed and said: "You're the same too — still smiling all the time."
He also told me he has two children, and the older one already goes to school.
We chatted for a long time, and in the end agreed to meet up often from now on.
One day in March, I discovered that last year's pants no longer fit.
My wife said with a smile: "You really have gotten fat."
I decided to start losing weight from that day on.
Now I go running in the park at six every morning, and I no longer eat cake or sweet things.
At first it was very hard — I was often both hungry and tired.
But after three months, I had lost five kilograms, and my health kept getting better and better.
Yesterday I put those pants on again, and my wife said I look much younger than before!
Last week I traveled to Beijing by myself and had a great time every day.
On Thursday morning, just as I was about to go to the bank to change money, I suddenly discovered my passport was lost!
I took everything out of my bag, but the passport wasn't there.
I searched the room for a long time — on the bed, under the table — and still couldn't find it.
I was extremely worried, because without a passport I wouldn't be able to fly home.
The hotel staff member said to me: "Don't worry, you can go ask at the nearby police station."
When I got to the police station, the officer asked me with a smile: "A taxi driver just brought in a passport — is it yours?"
It was exactly my passport! I was overjoyed and kept saying thank you to the officer.
